Job Summary

The Program Manager – Clean Energy Policy leads the coordination and execution of strategic clean energy, regulatory, and public policy initiatives impacting AVANGRID's Connecticut operating companies, including The United Illuminating Company (UI), Southern Connecticut Gas (SCG), and Connecticut Natural Gas (CNG). This role serves as a primary liaison across internal business units and external stakeholders to support the Companies' clean energy transition, grid modernization, affordability, resiliency, and decarbonization objectives.

This position is responsible for leading cross-functional efforts associated with Connecticut's Comprehensive Energy Strategy (CES), Performance-Based Regulation (PBR) proceedings, Equitable Modern Grid reopener program, electrification initiatives, and other DEEP and PURA regulatory matters. The Program Manager develops strategic recommendations, manages key regulatory deliverables, and supports engagement with state agencies, industry stakeholders, and executive leadership to advance AVANGRID's policy and business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

- Lead cross-functional coordination and strategic support for Connecticut DEEP, PURA, and legislative initiatives impacting UI, SCG, and CNG.

- Lead and coordinate Company participation in the CES and other statewide energy planning and decarbonization initiatives.

- Manage policy development and implementation activities related to PBR, Equitable Modern Grid Reopener, grid modernization, and utility transformation efforts.

- Support electrification strategies, including building decarbonization, transportation electrification, demand flexibility, and customer-focused clean energy programs.

- Develop strategic analyses, business cases, executive presentations, regulatory comments, testimony support, and briefing materials.

- Monitor emerging regulatory, legislative, and market developments and assess impacts on Company strategy, operations, and customers.

- Build and maintain strong working relationships with DEEP, PURA, Connecticut Green Bank, industry organizations, municipalities, and other key stakeholders.

- Lead complex regulatory projects across Regulatory, Rates, Planning, Operations, Customer Programs, Government Affairs, and Finance organizations, ensuring timely delivery of key commitments and objectives.

- Avangrid employees are assigned a system emergency role and in the event of a system emergency are expected to fulfill their assigned role.

- Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy development through implementation and benefits realization.

- Proven ability to develop business cases, evaluate program economics, and support investment and regulatory decision-making.

- Experience developing, communicating, and executing organizational, regulatory, or programmatic strategies that deliver measurable business results.

- Experience managing multiple priorities within a matrixed organization, including collaboration across geographically dispersed teams and stakeholders.

- Strong written, verbal, presentation, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to communicate effectively to executive leadership and external stakeholders.

- Experience supporting regulatory proceedings, including filings, testimony development, discovery responses, rate cases, and regulatory strategy execution.

- Master’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Public Policy, Business Administration (MBA), Economics, Energy Management, or a related field.

- Experience with electric and/or gas utility operations, customer programs, demand-side management, distributed energy resources (DERs), or grid modernization initiatives.

Job Summary:

The Director, Transmission/Interconnection is a key commercial and strategic role in Avangrid Power Transmission & Interconnection organization. Across all ISOs and RTOs in the United States, the Director will be responsible for developing and implementing interconnection and transmission strategies for energy projects; staying attuned to federal, state, ISO/RTO, and transmission owner rules for renewable generator interconnections; filing and negotiating new interconnection agreements; administering existing interconnection contracts including financial and operational terms and conditions; supporting the Senior Director in executive support activities, including financing, common facilities agreements, and FERC filings; and leading a team of Interconnection Analysts. A key part of the role will be managing relationships with ISO/RTO staff and specific third parties such as generators, utilities, public power entities, and selected large customers relative to transmission interconnections and service. Will work closely with all relevant departments at Avangrid Power by supporting development of power generation projects across the national ISO/RTO footprint.

Key Responsibilities:

- Collaborate with Avangrid Power Origination, Development, Project Delivery, Asset Management and Policy groups to align interconnection and transmission strategies and spend with greenfield development projects overall schedules.

- Develop and execute interconnection and transmission strategies across all U.S. ISOs and RTOs in support of Avangrid Renewables’ national business plan.

- Represent Avangrid Renewables’ transmission and interconnection strategy before transmission owners, ISOs/RTOs, and regulatory stakeholders across the country.

- Manage internal work procedures for interconnecting generators consistent with established Avangrid Renewables policy and business goals.

- Originating, negotiating and coordinating all new interconnection agreements, studies with ISO’s and third parties in accordance with regional tariffs and FERC orders.

- Management of existing interconnection agreements ensuring efficient and effective compliance with operational, financial and administrative terms and conditions.

- Support the Senior Director in executive-level activities, including financing readiness, common facilities agreement strategy and execution, and FERC filing support.

- Manage relationships with transmission owners and ISO/RTOS by participating in key conferences, boards, and taskforces to develop opportunities for collaboration.

- Regular collaboration meetings with key internal stakeholders to ensure alignment and timely information exchange.

- Lead and develop a team of interconnection analysts, providing coaching, performance feedback, and professional development to build technical capability and succession readiness.

- Set priorities, direct day-to-day work, and manage team workload and resources across regions to ensure timely, accurate execution of transmission and interconnection deliverables.

- Provide strategic direction to the team, ensuring coverage, technical support, and prioritization across all U.S. ISO/RTO regions as workload and business priorities require.

- Promote a collaborative, accountable team environment that supports knowledge sharing, cross-training, and consistent process execution.

Required Qualifications:

Technical Knowledge/Skill/Education/Licenses/Certifications:

- Demonstrated expertise in negotiation of interconnection agreements with consideration of a renewable projects’ overall schedule and risk profile.

- Thorough knowledge of ISO tariff procedures and schedule for generator interconnections, applicable engineering, work practices and procedures, and safety requirements.

- Knowledge of Federal, ISO, FERC and state interconnection, market and transmission development, planning, interconnection and operating procedures.

- Strong ability to understand and communicate complex issues in a simple and understandable manner verbally and in writing.

- Ability to communicate and work effectively with personnel at various levels within ISO, other transmission owners, members, and generation owners.

- Project management skills.

- Demonstrate expertise in relationship/team building and key stakeholder relationship building.

- Demonstrate ability to influence and lead others.

- Ability to work effectively with all levels of the Avangrid Power organization.

- Prior experience managing a team in the renewable energy space.

- Minimum of ten (10) years related experience.

- Prior experience representing or negotiating business interests with a developer, regional or industry organization.

- Experience developing competitive transmission or generation projects.

Job Summary

The Manager – Conservation & Load Management role is a dynamic, internally and externally visible role, responsible for leading the Finance, Reporting and Regulatory team within the Delivery of Conservation & Load Management ("CLM") Programs and Products team. The CLM team delivers high quality and cost-effective energy efficiency programs to natural gas and electricity customers in CT and MA, contributing to CT and MA clean energy goals and supporting a more sustainable electric and natural gas utility infrastructure. This position is expected to optimize the delivery of CLM products, programs, and services to exceed goals, and maximize customer, ratepayer and shareholder value by providing necessary finance, reporting and regulatory functions. This role is responsible for ensuring financial results and other stakeholder reporting are delivered accurately and on time, and the team and programs remain in compliance with regulatory obligations. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: management of the day-to-day operation of the Finance, Reporting and Regulatory team which includes coordination of work efforts, accountability for performance targets, oversight of budgeting, finance and accounting deliverables, oversight of regulatory deliverables, and the reporting and presentation of program performance results to internal and external stakeholders.

The Manager – Conservation & Load Mgmt role collaborates with both internal and external stakeholders to support the effective delivery of CLM programs and results. The Manager supervises and provides leadership and guidance to the Finance, Reporting and Regulatory team. Additionally, the Manager coordinates and provides effective identification, communication, prioritization, justification and documentation in the resolution of issues and projects within the Finance, Reporting and Regulatory processes of CLM, incorporating other functions within CLM and other company departments such as Finance, Accounting, Controls, Rates Customer Service, Regulatory, Operations, Legal, and other internal and external Strategic Business Partners. (This may include but is not limited to Eversource, CT EEB, MA EEAC, CT DEEP, CT PURA, MA DOER, Legislature, NEEP, etc.)
·         Support and advocate on behalf of the Company through testimony and discovery processes.

- Leverage strong knowledge of system capabilities to drive effective business processes

- Collaborate with multiple business areas including corporate Finance, Accounting, Controls, Rates, Regulatory, Legal, Customer Service, and other key business areas.

- Provide expertise and immediacy of decision making

- Effectively communicate with management/executives as well as at the front-line level to drive decisions with compliance front of mind.

·         Ensure that all activities and processes are in compliance with Sarbanes Oxley, Avangrid's business code of conduct, Rules of Employment and all other pertinent company policies.

·         Strong Business and Financial acumen
·         Proficient in in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Power Point applications
·         Leadership skills, analytical thought processes and the ability to work well with other groups across the Company

Job Description
This role provides transmission focused specialized technical expertise in power system studies by carrying out assignments associated with the modeling and development of the transmission system. The role requires experience associated with modeling, analyzing, and planning level designs of transmission lines and substation facilities in an electrical power system. Key responsibilities include performing steady state power flow analysis, short circuit studies, transient stability analysis and electromagnetic transient studies. The role includes responsibilities to develop and promote technical standards and represent the company regarding transmission planning matters at NPCC, NERC, NEPOOL, ISO-NE and MPUC.

Key Responsibilities

- Collaborate, perform, and lead reliability studies including power flow (thermal and voltage) analysis, transfer limit, short circuit, stability, and electromagnetic transient assessments.

- Analyze and assess complex transmission systems at numerous voltage levels.  Document and communicate results and recommendations as appropriate including data review, report writing, and summary presentations.

- Continually strive to innovate and integrate improvements to increase the precision and efficiency of transmission planning.

- Strive to seek out and develop subject matter expert skills as necessary to mentor and support the team to aid in the advancement of business needs.

- Collaborate and interact with internal teams and industry peers on regional activities (e.g. NPCC, ISO-NE, etc.).

- Develop and apply a thorough understanding of various planning criteria, guidelines, standards (e.g. NERC, NPCC, etc.) and analysis software packages such as PSS/E, TARA, EnFuzion, ASPEN, PSCAD, Python.

- Participate in transmission and substation site inspections; attend industry workshops, training, and user group meetings as needs arise.

- Assists during storm restoration as assigned.

Job Requirements

Behavioral Skills and Requirements

Behavioral Competencies

- Develop self & others

- Empower to grow

- Collaborate and share

- Be a role model

- Focus to achieve results

- Be agile

Technical Skills and Requirements
The following skills and associated competency levels are desired of those candidates seeking a position in Transmission Planning.  However, offsetting industry and other relevant technical skills will be considered for candidates without previous experience in these Transmission Planning activities (e.g. T&S Engineering, P&C, etc.).

Technical Skills/Competencies

- Theoretical Engineering knowledge: Planning, Operations and Engineering Design, Analytics, Modeling & Calculation (e.g. sym. Components, per unit, etc.), Understanding the Business Model

- Practical Engineering Experience/Application: Planning, Operations and Engineering Design, Construction, (e.g. field experience, standardization, developing business case and defend in front of stakeholders)

- Engineering documentation : Ability to adequately document and interpret engineering documentation, review and approve engineering work done by others

- Knowledge of Regulatory and Compliance Environment : Local, State and Federal Regulatory Standards and Requirements (NERC, NPCC, ISO, MPUC, etc.)

Functional Job Specific Competencies

- Power System Studies - Knowledge & Interpretation of Study Assumptions and Results : (e.g. Power Flow, Stability, Short Circuit, etc.)

- Software Proficiency - Power System Analytics: (e.g. PSSE, TARA, ASPEN, PSCAD, EnFuzion, Python)

Education & Experience Requirements:
Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
2-4 years of industry related experience OR 1 year of industry related experience with an industry related Master’s degree
PE recommended

Job Summary

Lead, AI Change Management is responsible for leading transformation change management activities that enable business adoption of digital, data, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled ways of working across the utility enterprise.  This role partners with business stakeholders, Data & AI, Enterprise Architecture, People & Organization, Communications, Legal/Compliance, Talent, and Information Technology to assess change impacts, design adoption strategies, build stakeholder alignment, and ensure sustainable adoption of transformation initiatives. This role translates transformation goals into practical change plans, communication and training approaches, readiness metrics, and stakeholder engagement activities that drive measurable value realization while supporting responsible AI adoption and risk-aware change practices.

Key Responsibilities

Transformation change strategy & execution: Develop and execute structured change management strategies for enterprise transformation initiatives, including digital, data, process, and AI-enabled programs; define change approach, roadmap, adoption plan, and success measures.

AI change management & responsible adoption: Lead change activities that help employees understand, trust, and effectively adopt AI capabilities, including role-based impacts, responsible use expectations, human-in-the-loop practices, model limitations, privacy, security, and governance requirements.

Stakeholder engagement & alignment: Identify and manage stakeholder groups across operations, customer, corporate functions, OT, IT, HR, legal/compliance, and leadership; facilitate engagement sessions, readiness discussions, and feedback loops to secure alignment and reduce adoption risk. Develop and manage business change champion and AI ambassador networks to accelerate adoption, gather feedback, identify resistance, and promote best-practice sharing across the enterprise.

Change impact assessment & readiness: Assess current-state processes, operating model impacts, role changes, skills gaps, adoption barriers, and resistance points; translate findings into readiness plans, mitigation actions, and targeted interventions. Integrate change management activities into agile delivery, product development, release management, and business deployment processes to ensure adoption planning begins early in the initiative's lifecycle.

Communications & training enablement: Partner with Communications, P & O, business leaders, and program teams to develop clear messaging, leadership talking points, training materials, user guides, office hours, and adoption campaigns that support successful transition.
Business process redesign & adoption support: Support process redesign and operating model changes needed to embed transformation outcomes into day-to-day work; coordinate with business teams to align procedures, controls, accountabilities, and adoption milestones.

Metrics, value realization & adoption monitoring: Define and track change adoption KPIs, including stakeholder readiness, training completion, usage, proficiency, satisfaction, behavior change, operational impact, and value realization; prepare executive-ready reporting and insights. Analyze user adoption patterns using platform telemetry, survey feedback, training participation, and business KPIs to identify adoption gaps and recommend targeted interventions.

Risk, governance & compliance partnership: Embed change management into governance checkpoints and project lifecycles; coordinate with AI governance, legal/compliance, cybersecurity, privacy, and risk teams to ensure adoption plans reflect applicable policies and controls.

Sustainment & continuous improvement: Support pilot-to-production transitions, adoption reinforcement, lessons learned, continuous improvement cycles, and post-implementation sustainment plans to ensure transformation benefits are realized and maintained.

AI literacy and workforce capability development: Partner with business leaders, HR/P&O, and learning teams to develop AI literacy programs, role-based learning pathways, AI champion networks, and workforce upskilling initiatives that improve organizational readiness and AI fluency.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science or a related field of study and eight (8) years of relevant experience.

- Relevant experience includes leading organizational change, transformation, business process improvement, digital adoption, or enterprise program implementation in complex environments.

- Experience supporting cross-functional transformation initiatives that require stakeholder alignment, communications, training, readiness planning, and adoption measurement.

- Prior experience with change management, business transformation, process redesign, communications, learning/adoption, operations, or technology-enabled program delivery.

- Ability to build change strategies, impact assessments, stakeholder maps, readiness plans, resistance mitigation actions, adoption plans, and sustainment approaches.

- Encompasses a practical understanding of responsible AI adoption, human-centered change, data privacy, model risk, explainability, security, and governance concepts as they relate to employee adoption.

- Proven ability to facilitate cross-functional workshops, align diverse stakeholder groups, and translate complex transformation topics into clear, audience-specific messages.

- Ability to partner with communications, HR, business leaders, and program teams to create launch materials, role-based training, office hours, and adoption campaigns.

- Capability to define adoption metrics, usage indicators, behavior-change measures, readiness dashboards, and executive reporting that connect change activity to business outcomes.

- Prior experience supporting pilots, release planning, transition activities, operational handoffs, post-go-live reinforcement, and continuous improvement for transformation initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications

- Prior experience with data/AI within utility operations.

- Experience in power and utilities, energy, infrastructure, regulated industries, or heavy asset industries.

- Familiarity with change management methodologies such as Prosci ADKAR, Kotter, agile change, design thinking, or human-centered adoption practices.
